question: Japan's 1978 computer character set held dozens of characters no dictionary recorded. Where did one of them, 妛, come from?
answer: From a paste-up. A place name wrote 山 stacked above 女 as a single character. Compilers pasted the two printed pieces onto a sheet, and on the copy the edge where the paper met read as a stroke. So 妛 entered the standard, and later Unicode: a character born from a paper edge.
move: An official list can preserve a clerk's error as faithfully as a fact.
reference: Japanese Standards Association, JIS X 0208:1997, 7-bit and 8-bit double byte coded Kanji sets for information interchange, Annex 7, 1997
